Related follow-up for anyone tracking this issue: I just filed #41354 — "Search across my message history to quickly locate past conversations/content".

Short version: `Ctrl+F` here solves "find in the session I'm looking at", but with hundreds of sessions across many projects, the recurring problem is **finding which session contains a phrase I typed weeks ago** ("what did I tell the agent before"). No content search over the session store exists today — the only workaround is recalling the approximate title and scrolling.

A cross-session search (user messages, filterable by project/date, results jump into the matched session) is the natural complement to this issue — and if/when this in-session Find lands, the cross-session results can reuse it to scroll straight to the matched message. Just adding that context here for whoever picks this up.

Same pain point here — supporting this one.

User scenario (desktop app, Windows): when an MCP server fails to start (or a remote one drops), the client stays in a broken/stale state and the **only** working recovery is a full app relaunch. There is no visible "reconnect" affordance in the UI and no retry button; the status stays stale until relaunch, exactly as this issue describes.

This is the desktop-side half of the MCP resilience family — the other open issues I've found:
- #25287 (no transport-level retry on socket errors)
- #38266 (local stdio MCP silently dropped mid-session)
- #36581 (managed reconnect waits until fourth failure)
- #36582 (make API failures explicit and actionable)

For desktop users specifically, a per-MCP status indicator with a manual "Reconnect/Retry" action (even if auto-reconnect stays conservative) would cover the cases auto-retry can't, without waiting for a full relaunch. Adding this here since stale-state-until-relaunch is the exact symptom.
As a Chinese-speaking Windows desktop user, +1. The English-only UI adds friction for me daily; auto-detect system locale is the best approach.
Free-tier / pay-as-you-go users need this visibility most, especially to decide when to compact. I'd also settle for the /usage command (Option 2) as the MVP.

Same pain here — hundreds of sessions stay labeled "New session..." in the sidebar, which also makes finding past conversations harder (I filed #41354 about cross-session search). Auto-title from the first prompt helps both.

I couldn't reproduce this as a prerelease-semver resolution failure. Using Bun 1.3.11 (`af24e281`) against the public npm registry, both exact Windows packages resolve successfully:

```sh
bun add --lockfile-only @opencode-ai/cli-windows-x64@0.0.0-next-17055
bun add --lockfile-only @opencode-ai/cli-windows-x64-baseline@0.0.0-next-17055
```

The version was published shortly before this report. Also, the successful npm command explicitly forces `registry.npmjs.org`, while the failing Bun command does not. That points to stale package metadata in Bun's cache or a configured registry mirror/proxy, rather than Bun rejecting the `-next` version.

Could you please try:

```sh
bun pm cache rm
bun add -g --trust @opencode-ai/cli@next --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
```

If it still fails, please share whether a registry is configured in `bunfig.toml` (redacting any credentials). That will distinguish a Windows-specific Bun resolver problem from stale registry metadata.

Additional data points from our debugging:
- Trigger: any caller that POSTs a prompt with format: json_schema - we hit it via the opencode-mem plugin v2.24.3 (auto-capture and user-profile learning both call session.prompt with structured output). Related: tickernelz/opencode-mem#226.
- The message with the bad format is not persisted to the DB (no format key in any message row), so the 400 comes from the server's read-back/encode path - consistent with the Schema.Class vs plain-object diagnosis.
- In the Desktop UI this means every session load fails with 400 while such a message exists in server memory - not just API clients.

PR #37541 already contains the fix (wire schemas changed from Schema.Class to Schema.Struct) with the regression test passing and a verified Windows build - but it has sat unreviewed/unmerged since Jul 17. People are actively hitting this. Can we get it reviewed and merged?

- This issue is about **within-session staleness** (todo stuck on one item for several turns while the agent already moved past it) and the **task-switch reset** case (new task → old todo list remains displayed and referenced), plus the ask that todowrite slots be refreshed each turn as part of the agent loop.

The closed #28961/#38516/#33063 relate to the same family, so I've consolidated the remaining open gaps here rather than opening more. Keep this open as the actionable track (assigned); happy to retitle to "todo list lifecycle: stale tracking + task-switch reset" if that matches maintainer naming conventions.

Additional implementation/testing context:

- `packages/core/src/shell.ts` discovers Windows candidates with `which("pwsh")` and `which("powershell")`. Rooted paths are accepted only when `stat(...).isFile()` succeeds, and `Shell.list()` filters candidates through that resolution.
- `packages/core/test/shell.test.ts` has Windows coverage for normal shell resolution, including bare PowerShell when `which("pwsh")` returns a regular path, but it does not cover `Shell.list()` with a Windows App Execution Alias or an MSIX installation.

A fix should preserve validation for normal executable paths while handling App Execution Aliases, with a Windows-specific regression test if feasible.

@Raynos thanks — that's a useful second data point, and it widens the reported surface. My evidence was GLM-5.2; deepseek V4 flash hitting the same stall says this isn't provider-specific, which is what I'd expect from the mechanism.

The stall you describe is the shape this PR targets. Before the change, `finish === "length"` fell through the loop-exit condition at `prompt.ts` as an ordinary completion, so a turn truncated mid-work ended the loop with no error and no continuation — the subagent looks like it finished. After it, a truncated turn that produced usable text or tool calls gets exactly one continuation, and a reasoning-only truncation surfaces `OutputLengthError` instead of exiting silently. Either way the caller learns something happened.

One caveat worth stating: the continuation is bounded to a single attempt (the previous turn's `finish` is the bound, so no loop state is added). If a model truncates repeatedly, you get the error rather than an unbounded retry — deliberate, since auto-continuing without a bound is a money pump.

On the bot's suggestion of #26167 — I looked, and they're adjacent but not overlapping. #26167 handles an upstream stream ending with no proper `stop_reason` (a fallback finish with zero output tokens) and makes that retryable in the processor. This one handles a well-formed `length` finish that the loop classified as normal completion. Different input condition, different layer: the only shared file is `prompt.ts`, and the hunks are in different functions — theirs threads a `priorOutput` flag into `processor.create`, mine changes the loop-exit condition and the entry gate. They should merge cleanly in either order.

If your deepseek case has a log line showing the finish reason on the stalling turn, that would be worth adding here — it'd confirm the same `length` path rather than the zero-token fallback #26167 covers.

## Confirmed write-path still open on `dev`: full `patch` in `message.summary.diffs`

This is **measurements / storage shape only** — not a proposed redesign.

### What is still broken on current `dev`

`SessionSummary.summarize()` still assigns the full `Snapshot.diffFull()` result (including complete `patch` text) onto the user message:

```ts
target.info.summary = { ...target.info.summary, diffs: msgDiffs }
```

That payload is durable and is re-emitted on every step-finish via `message.updated.1`, so it multiplies through the append-only `event` table.

Earlier PRs that stripped this (`#32410`, `#33892`) were **auto-closed by cleanup**, never merged. `upstream/dev` still has no `compactSummaryDiffs` (or equivalent) on the summarize write path.

Related filed issue with DB/event growth: #32005.

### Local evidence (one toxic session)

| Artifact | Size / observation |
|---|---|
| Single user `message.summary.diffs` | ~136 MB (full patch text) |
| `event` rows for that session | ~6.2 GB |
| `opencode.db` before sanitize | ~7.4 GB (`event` ~6.8 GB) |
| After stripping fat `summary.diffs` / fat events | DB ~1.2 GB |
| Process symptom | macOS Jetsam; `opencode` RSS reported in the tens of GiB while WAL dirty writes were enormous |

Also saw vendor / `.node-runtime` trees included in those diffs, which makes the stored patches pathological even when the edited source itself is small.

### Why a heap-only reading of #20695 can miss this

JS heap snapshots help for in-process retention of `FileDiff` strings (already reported earlier in this thread by others). This path additionally blows **SQLite `event` / `message` durability**, so reopen / fanout / Jetsam can happen even when a single JS heap sample looks “only” a few GB — the durable log is the amplifier.

### Temporary mitigation (until a core fix lands)

Plugin + sanitizer workaround (caps/denies vendor diffs on the chat transform path, spills fat events, optional DB sanitize). **Not a core write-path fix** — the engine can still persist full patches; this only reduces damage in practice:

https://github.com/KirillDeviatka/opencode-session-diff-spill

### Open fix PR (TypeScript, same codebase — not a rewrite)

#40861 — store lightweight metadata only (`file` / status / additions / deletions), drop vendor / `.node-runtime` / `dist` paths from durable summaries, recompute full patches on demand via existing `diff()` / `computeDiff()`.

Local verification:

```text
bun test test/session/summary-diffs.test.ts   # pass (incl. size regression)
bun run typecheck                             # packages/opencode — pass
```

Happy to rebase if a complementary path-scoping change lands first (#40821). Maintainer CI approval is still needed on #40861 (first-time contributor workflows gated).

## Root cause found (with reproducible evidence): silent `small_model` failure, swallowed and never retried

Following up on my earlier comment from July 6 where I hypothesized a UI/race bug — I dug into the logs and found the actual cause. It's not intermittent, it's deterministic, and it's a config/provider issue masquerading as a missing feature.

### The mechanism

Title generation runs exactly once per session, right after the first user message (`ensureTitle` in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`). It resolves the model as: the `title` agent's model, else `small_model` from config, else the session model. If the LLM call fails, the error is **swallowed by `Effect.ignore`** (`prompt.ts:1139`) and **never retried** — on the next user message, `history.filter(real).length !== 1` is false, so `ensureTitle` returns early forever. The session keeps `New session - <timestamp>` for life.

Subagent sessions are unaffected because their title is set synchronously at creation (`... (@agent subagent)`), bypassing the `title` agent entirely — which is exactly the pattern I reported on July 6 (1/15 sessions titled, the titled one being a subagent dispatch).

### The evidence

Grepping my local opencode.db (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`), every untitled top-level session had a matching error in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`:

```
level=ERROR message="stream error" providerID=fireworks modelID=glm-4p7-flash small=true agent=title error.error="AI_APICallError: Model not found, inaccessible, and/or not deployed"
```

One `stream error` per untitled session, all naming the same `small_model`. In my case this had **two layers**:
1. `small_model` pointed at `fireworks/glm-4p7-flash`, a model id Fireworks had retired (404 `Model not found`).
2. The deeper blocker: the Fireworks account itself was **suspended for billing** (412 `Account ... is suspended, possibly due to reaching the monthly spending limit`). My main model ran on a different provider (OpenRouter), so the app worked fine — only `small_model` (on Fireworks) failed, silently, taking the session titles down with it.

### The fix (user-side)

Point `small_model` at a live, independent provider. In `opencode.json`:

```json
"small_model": "openrouter/inclusionai/ling-2.6-flash"
```

Cost is negligible (~0.01 USD/year for ~10 sessions/day). After restart, new sessions auto-title and the sidebar is usable again. I backfilled 21 past untitled sessions by generating a title from each session's first user message and updating `session.title` directly in the DB.

### Suggestion for maintainers

The user-visible symptom ("wall of New session") is caused by a config/provider problem, but the **fragility is in the title path itself**:

1. **No retry.** Title generation fires once and only once. If the LLM call fails for any transient reason (rate limit, timeout, a flaky small_model id, billing suspension), the session is permanently untitled. A retry on the next user message (relax the `history.filter(real).length !== 1` guard to `=== 1` on first attempt, or retry while `isDefaultTitle` is true) would recover most of these cases.
2. **Silent failure.** `Effect.ignore` on the forked title fiber means the error never surfaces — not even in the TUI. Logging the title failure (or surfacing a one-time warning when `isDefaultTitle` is still true after N messages) would make this self-diagnosable instead of a GitHub ticket.

The diagnostic recipe for anyone hitting this: `rg "agent=title" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` — if you see `stream error` lines, your `small_model` (or its provider account) is the culprit, not the title feature.

On the source-level replacement: agreed that it is a reasonable belt-and-braces follow-up. I kept this PR at the invalid-tool boundary intentionally so the behavior is centralized for the invalid tool path and stays narrowly focused on removing the repeated `Available tools:` enumeration.

Thanks! Yes, that fallback is intentional.

The generated config schema root is expected to be an object today, so the useful compatibility fix is to inline the resolved object root and expose `type` / `properties` directly for JSON language servers. If the root `$ref` ever resolved to a non-object definition, preserving the original `$ref` is safer than manufacturing an object-shaped root or dropping semantics. In other words, the fallback is defensive rather than support for an expected array/enum config root.

Thanks for tracing that — that matches what I saw.

I confirmed the direct Anthropic path is not rewritten through the common shape: `createBodyConverter()` returns the original body unchanged when `from === to`. So an Anthropic request going to an Anthropic provider still keeps the native `input_schema` wire shape.

The flat `{ name, description, parameters }` shape introduced here is only the intermediate CommonRequest representation used when converting Anthropic input to another output format, specifically the Anthropic -> OpenAI-compatible path covered by the regression test.

Two commits added since the original description, both worth calling out because the second one is a defect this PR would otherwise have shipped.

**`45dc93b083`** — regression test for the notify/background consumer. The original tests only covered the foreground `Effect.fail` exit; the `inject("error", …)` exit got the same operator change untested. That is the path the reported incident actually came through, so it should not have been the untested one.

**`60b30f1353`** — a real bug in the first commit. Effect's `TimeoutError` is `instanceof Error` but its `message` is `undefined`, not a string, so `error.message.trim()` threw a `TypeError` inside `BackgroundJob.settle`. The job then never settled and `background.wait()` hung indefinitely. Fixed with `typeof` guards on `.message` and `.name`, matching the guard already on `_tag`.

Worth being explicit about why CI did not catch that: it could not. There is no test on `dev` that routes a `TimeoutError` through `settle`, so the suite is green and correct. It surfaced on a downstream branch that has a task-timeout feature and therefore exercises that path. The regression test added here builds the error from the real producer rather than a hand-made `{ message: undefined }` object — I checked that `new Cause.TimeoutError()` matches what an actual `Effect.timeout` emits (same constructor, `_tag`, and `typeof message`), so the fixture pins the production shape.

On completeness of the guard, since "add a typeof check" invites "what else is unguarded": the two mechanisms that produce a blank or non-string message here are disjoint and both covered. Effect built-ins with `message === undefined` (`TimeoutError`, `NoSuchElementError`, `ExceededCapacityError`, `IllegalArgumentError`, `UnknownError`) all carry a string `_tag`, so the second rung catches them. Tagged errors defined in this repo inherit `message: ""` from `Error.prototype`, so the string check passes, `trim()` is falsy, and they also fall through to `_tag`. Verified against `effect@4.0.0-beta.83`.

There is a residual: a non-`Error` value with a throwing `toString` or `Symbol.toPrimitive` can still make the final `String(error)` throw. I left it alone — it is not producible by Effect or by anything in this repo, and wrapping the function in try/catch to cover it would hide the next real shape the way the missing guard hid this one.

Added `a75423f94d`, fixing a bug in the `timeout` feature this PR introduces: a task that failed terminally left the child's agent loop running.

The child kept calling the model and running tools after the parent had already received its error frame, and no tool could stop it — `task_abort` refuses on a settled job, so the child was unreachable. Measured on a live build before the fix:

```
child dispatched with timeout: 25000, heartbeat every ~7.4s
parent received the error frame at ~25s
child continued to 20/20 ticks — 145s of work, 120s past the parent's frame
task_abort issued mid-way -> "has already finished"
```

`Effect.onInterrupt` fires on interruption only. Probed against this repo's Effect version:

```
typed failure (Effect.fail)  -> does not fire
Effect.timeout               -> does not fire
Effect.die                   -> does not fire
Effect.interrupt             -> fires
```

The child's loop is forked into the per-instance scope in `effect/runner.ts` and the caller only awaits a `Deferred`, so `Effect.timeout` interrupts the await, not the run fiber. The `run` passed to `background.start` is wrapped in `Effect.onInterrupt(() => ops.cancel(childID))`, which covers parent abort but never fires on a terminal failure — so nothing cancelled the runner.

The fix moves the existing `ops.cancelRun(childID)` call so it runs on any failure exit rather than only on the fallback path. `cancelRun` is the runner-only interrupt that skips `cancelBackgroundJobs`, so it cannot self-cancel the enclosing job.

A comment I added in the original timeout work was wrong and is replaced:

```diff
-// No ops.cancel here: Effect.timeout already interrupted the ops.prompt fiber,
+// Timeout interrupts the await, not the child runner; cancelRun stops that
+// runner without canceling the enclosing background job.
```

`Effect.timeout` did interrupt a fiber — just not the one that mattered.

Verification: red-first, and the mutation check removes only the new call. Both the new regression test and the pre-existing fallback test go red, so the single call now covers both paths. The prior `timeout without fallback fails the task` test passed with the bug present, since it only asserted the tool returned a failure; the new assertion is that the child's runner was actually cancelled.

```
task suite   44 pass / 0 fail
full suite   3289 pass / 0 fail
typecheck    clean
mutation     42 pass / 2 fail with the call removed
```

One behaviour worth stating precisely, since the placement suggests otherwise: the new call does not execute on parent abort. The outer fiber is being interrupted at that point, so the `yield*` is skipped — `onInterrupt` already handles that path. Cross-family review confirmed this empirically rather than by inspection.

## Request for clarification: how model usage maps to Go quota limits

Thank you for investigating this. I would like to clarify the accounting model behind the Go limits, because the numbers in this issue appear to show that the dollar amounts in Usage History are not the same dollar amounts used by the rolling, weekly, and monthly quota counters.

According to the [OpenCode Go documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/en/go/#usage-limits), the plan limits are:

- 5-hour limit: **$12 of usage**
- Weekly limit: **$30 of usage**
- Monthly limit: **$60 of usage**

The documentation says that these limits are defined in dollar value, and that the number of requests depends on the model. It also provides an estimated request-count table for each model. However, it is not clear whether the dollar amounts shown in the Usage History are the exact dollar values deducted from these quota windows, or whether Go applies a separate internal normalization, multiplier, model weight, or other accounting rule.

### Numbers from this issue

The Usage History in this report shows approximately:

- DeepSeek V4 Pro: $2.01
- GPT-5.6 Luna: $6.46
- DeepSeek V4 Pro: $0.04
- Qwen3.8 Max: $2.58
- Total visible Go usage: approximately **$11.09**

The quota dashboard simultaneously shows:

- Rolling usage: **87%**
- Weekly usage: **100%**
- Monthly usage: **52%**

If the visible Usage History amounts were used directly, $11.09 would correspond to approximately:

- $11.09 / $30 = **37%** of the weekly limit, not 100%
- $11.09 / $60 = **18.5%** of the monthly limit, not 52%

The monthly value of 52% corresponds to approximately $31.20 of internal monthly quota usage, despite only $11.09 being visible in Usage History. The weekly value shows an even larger discrepancy, because the weekly window is already exhausted.

### Related concrete examples

Other reports show the same pattern:

- [Issue #41146](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/41146) reports approximately **$7.52** of visible `qwen3.8-max` usage, while the **$30 weekly limit** is at 100% and the **$60 monthly limit** is at 50%.
- [Issue #40031](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/40031) reports approximately **$3** of visible Grok usage, while the session usage is shown as 100% of a **$12** rolling limit.
- [Issue #38936](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/38936) reports approximately **$20** of visible usage, while the **$60 monthly** quota is shown as fully exhausted.

These examples suggest that the quota system may be charging an internal usage amount that is different from the user-visible Usage History amount. They also suggest that the relationship may be model-dependent.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40736: Reports the same cross-session file diff contamination — concurrent sessions in the same worktree cause one session's diff to include file changes made by another session. That issue also identifies the snapshot isolation as the root cause and proposes a similar fix.

Confirming this independently, and adding one detail about the second half — the misleading prompt path — because it is worse than cosmetic.

The containment check is `FSUtil.contains`, which is `path.relative` plus a `..` test, so it is purely lexical:

```
worktree  /tmp/symlink-probe/proj
link      /tmp/symlink-probe/proj/link -> /tmp/symlink-probe/secret

contains(worktree, "proj/link/creds.txt")   -> true    (lexically inside)
contains(worktree, "secret/creds.txt")      -> false   (correctly outside)
```

Same file, two paths, opposite verdicts.

The part worth adding: the path that reaches the permission matcher is the relativized one, so an absolute deny rule on the real location cannot match it.

```
permissionPath(via symlink) -> "link/creds.txt"
realpath                     -> /tmp/symlink-probe/secret/creds.txt
```

A rule like `/tmp/symlink-probe/secret/**: deny` is evaluated against `link/creds.txt` and does not match. So this is not only a missing `external_directory` prompt — an explicit deny rule covering the symlink's target is silently inert for access through the link. A user who has denied a sensitive directory still gets the read.

Verified on `dev`. `permissionPath` lives in `packages/opencode/src/project/instance-context.ts`; `FSUtil.contains` in `packages/core/src/fs-util.ts`.

Worth noting that `realpath` is not a free fix: resolving on every check costs a syscall per permission evaluation, and resolving only the containment check while leaving the emitted path lexical would fix the prompt-absence half but leave the deny-rule half broken. Both halves want the resolved path, which also changes what users see in prompts for legitimately symlinked project layouts.
